poster_title: Evaluating LLM Agents as Lifelong Learners
authors: Junhao Zheng, Xidi Cai, Qiuke Li, Duzhen Zhang, Zhong-Zhi Li, Yingying Zhang, Le Song, Qianli Ma
paper_info: 2023, South China University of Technology, MBZUAI, Chinese Academy of Sciences, East China Normal University

panels.headline: Rapid development of LLMs and shift to LLM-based agents.
content: Rapid development of large language models (LLMs) has revolutionized language-based AI.
Research has shifted to LLM-based agents that interact with dynamic environments and perform complex decision-making.
Existing benchmarks fail to evaluate lifelong learning capabilities in LLM agents.
Lifelong learning is crucial for LLM agents to adapt and improve over time.
This work introduces a new benchmark for lifelong learning in LLM agents.

panels.headline: No standardized benchmark for lifelong learning in LLM agents.
content: LLM-based agents lack memory and the ability to incrementally accumulate knowledge over time.
No standardized benchmark for evaluating lifelong learning in LLM agents.
Label inaccuracies, lack of verifiability, and poor reproducibility in prior benchmarks.
panels.figure_caption: Comparison between LifelongAgentBench and existing benchmarks. † : [19] highlights label error issues in WebArena.

panels.headline: Introduction of LifelongAgentBench with four key properties.
content: Introduction of LifelongAgentBench, a unified benchmark for evaluating lifelong learning in LLM agents.
Tasks are skill-grounded and explicitly designed to measure inter-task relatedness.
Automatic label verification and a fully containerized infrastructure for reproducibility.
Modular design with extensible callback functions and a pluggable LLM agent interface.
panels.figure_caption: Overview of LifelongAgentBench : a unified dataset and evaluation framework with skillgrounded tasks, modular components, and four key properties: task dependency, label verifiability, reproducibility, and modularity.

panels.headline: Evaluation of experience replay effectiveness.
content: Tasks across three interactive environments: Database (DB), Operating System (OS), and Knowledge Graph (KG).
Evaluation of experience replay effectiveness in different model sizes, architectures, and task complexities.
Introduction of a group self-consistency mechanism to improve decision quality.

panels.headline: Group self-consistency significantly enhances experience replay.
content: Conventional experience replay has limited effectiveness due to irrelevant information and context length constraints.
Group self-consistency mechanism significantly enhances the effectiveness of experience replay across multiple LLM backbones.
panels.figure_caption: Skill distributions across tasks. Diverse and balanced skill coverage is maintained.

panels.headline: LifelongAgentBench advances the development of adaptive, memory-capable LLM agents.
content: LifelongAgentBench advances the development of adaptive, memory-capable LLM agents.
Group self-consistency mechanism is a promising approach to enhance lifelong learning.
The benchmark provides a systematic analysis of lifelong learning limitations in LLM agents.
The effectiveness of experience replay varies significantly across different models and tasks.
Future work can explore more sophisticated lifelong learning strategies.
The modular design of LifelongAgentBench allows for easy extension and customization.
